Shelby County by the numbers

Where do I record a deed in Shelby County, and when is the office open?

Deeds for Shelby County land are recorded by the Register of Deeds. The main office is at 1075 Mullins Station Road, Building W-3, in Memphis, TN 38134, and the mailing address uses Suite W165. The FAQ on the register's website gives office hours from 8:00 in the morning until 4:15 in the afternoon on weekdays, with a phone line at 901-222-8100. Willie F. Brooks, Jr. has held the elected post since August 5, 2022.

Two other counter locations, Downtown Memphis and Southbrook, appear on the home page. A notice there shut both for a lunch-hour stretch on Friday, November 13, 2026, which has already passed, and pointed in-person filers to a drop box at the Mullins Station office. Payment can be made with cash, a cashier's check, a money order, a business check or most major credit cards.

The staff records documents and cannot help draft them or give legal advice. The office also has no notary for the public, so a seller should have the deed signed and notarized before it arrives, often at a bank.

What should a Shelby County seller know about the county itself?

Shelby County sits in the far southwest corner of Tennessee, bounded on the west by the Mississippi River and on the south by Mississippi's DeSoto and Marshall counties. At 781.6 square miles it is the state's largest county by area, and Memphis is both the county seat and the largest city. The county was formed in 1819, and the courthouse moved to Memphis in 1868 after years at Raleigh, now absorbed into the city.

Six incorporated places share the county with Memphis: Bartlett, Germantown, Lakeland and Millington as cities, plus Arlington and Collierville as towns. In 2014 Arlington, Bartlett, Collierville, Germantown, Lakeland and Millington formed their own school districts, while Shelby County Schools serves Memphis and most unincorporated areas. A seller's school zone therefore depends on which municipality the house sits in.

U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts gives this snapshot:

  • 910,226 people in July 2025, down 2.1% from the April 2020 base
  • 409,202 housing units, with an owner-occupied rate of 54.1%
  • A typical owner-occupied home valued at $249,100 for 2020 to 2024
  • Median gross rent of $1,232 and median household income of $63,767
  • 1,230 building permits in 2025

With fewer than six in ten homes owner-occupied, rental and investor sales are a large share of the Shelby market, and the register's fee schedule applies the same way to each of them.

What does the Shelby County register require before it records a deed?

The register's filing guidelines list the items a taxable deed needs, with the Tennessee Code section beside each. Missing any of them can lead to rejection, so a title company or attorney usually checks the list. The core items are:

  • Grantor and grantee names, with proper acknowledgments (T.C.A. 66-22-101)
  • An affidavit of value when the deed is taxable (67-4-409)
  • A derivation clause pointing to the prior recorded deed (66-24-110)
  • The property address unless the land is vacant (66-24-113)
  • Name and address of the owner and of whoever pays the property tax (66-24-114)
  • Ward, block and parcel number (66-24-122)
  • Name and address of the person who prepared it (66-24-115)
  • The legal description, and an original signed document unless it is e-filed

The office says that once a document meets the minimum legal requirements and the fees are paid, it is recorded and returned within about one business day by mail. A digital copy appears on the website as well.

What will a Shelby County deed cost to file?

Two charges apply to a sale deed: a recording fee and the state realty transfer tax. The recording fee is $12.00 for up to two pages on the register's fee schedule, which matches the $10.00 page fee plus a $2.00 fee the guidelines itemize. Each added page costs $5.00. The tax is $0.37 per $100 of the greater of price or value, and the register adds $1.00 whenever state tax is collected.

The register's own example puts the tax on a $100,000 sale at $370. At Shelby's $249,100 typical home value, the tax would be about $921.67. A quitclaim deed is the exception: its tax depends only on the actual consideration given.

Shelby County recording charges listed by the Register of Deeds
ItemChargeSource
Warranty or quitclaim deed, up to 2 pages$12.00Shelby Register fee schedule
Each added page$5.00Shelby Register fee schedule
Realty transfer tax$0.37 per $100Filing guidelines
Mortgage tax$0.115 per $100, first $2,000 exemptFee schedule
Certified copy$1.00 per pageFee schedule
Plain copy at the counter$0.50 per page ($1.50 for plats)Register FAQ

A buyer who overpays transfer or mortgage tax must ask the Tennessee Department of Revenue, not the register, for a refund. The request needs copies of the instruments, the tax receipts, a short statement of the reason and a claim form, plus a Report of Debt form for refunds above $200.

Which Shelby County transfers owe no transfer tax?

The guidelines list a set of transfers that carry no realty transfer tax, and no oath of value is needed on them. Common examples for a family selling or retitling a house are:

  • A deed between spouses that creates or ends a tenancy by the entirety
  • A deed an executor signs to carry out a will
  • A divorce decree or deed that adjusts property rights between the parties
  • A transfer into or out of a revocable living trust by the same owner or spouse
  • A trustee's deed that distributes real estate to trust beneficiaries

An ordinary arm's-length sale to a buyer is taxable. A seller who is unsure how a transfer is classified should ask the closing attorney before the deed is signed.

Can a Shelby County seller e-file, or must the deed go in by mail?

Individuals cannot e-file in Shelby County. State law effective July 1, 2025 (T.C.A. 47-10-118) limits electronic filing to licensed attorneys, banks, credit unions, federally backed lenders, regulated lenders, title insurers and agents, and government bodies. Each e-filed document also needs an electronic certification form under T.C.A. 66-24-101.

The register adds that account setup can take 48 hours or longer, so most sellers rely on the title company's existing account. Frequent filers can open an escrow account so shortages are drawn and overages credited automatically. Account forms go to 1075 Mullins Station Road, W-165, Memphis, TN 38134.

Property owners can also join the register's Property Fraud Alert program, which notifies them when a threat to their title appears.

What if the Shelby County owner has died or the loan was just paid off?

For an owner who has died, the register points families to the Shelby County Probate Court Clerk at 901-222-3750 to learn whether a will was probated. If one was, it may serve as the deed. If not, an Affidavit of Heirship is recorded, at $10.00 for the first two pages plus the $2.00 fee. Title companies usually want three affidavits from three witnesses, two of whom are unrelated to the family.

A payoff produces a trust deed release, which the register can locate for the owner. Lien searches are not the register's job, because some liens sit in court files instead of the land records.

How does recording a deed relate to Shelby County property tax?

Recording moves title but does not clear a tax bill. Ask the Shelby County Trustee for the status of the current and any past-due bills before closing, and ask the Assessor of Property, Javier Bailey, Sr., how the parcel is valued. The state's assessment calendar, as published by the Sumner County assessor, shows that Shelby's county board of equalization convenes on May 1, a month earlier than other counties, so an appeal here has an earlier clock.

More questions about Shelby County, TN Register of Deeds

How long does Shelby County take to record a deed?

About one business day. The register says it records the deed and mails it back in roughly that time, and a digital copy is posted to its website.

Can I record my own deed online in Shelby County?

No. The register has no e-filing option for individuals, and state law limits electronic submission to attorneys, banks, lenders, title companies and government bodies. Use a title company or attorney with an account, or mail or bring the original.

What does recording a quitclaim deed cost in Shelby County?

The register says a quitclaim typically costs $12 to file for up to two pages. Tax, if due, is based only on the consideration given, at $0.37 per $100.

Does the Shelby County register help fill out deeds?

No. The office is a recording office only and cannot give legal advice or help complete forms. It also has no notary for the public, so arrange notarization before you go.

How do I get a copy of my Shelby County deed?

Search the register's website first, since many recorded documents can be viewed and copied free. Otherwise ask in person, by email or by mail with names, a date or the property address. Counter copies cost $0.50 a page.

Knox County by the numbers

Where is the Knox County Register of Deeds, and what does it do?

The office is at 400 Main Street, Suite 225, Knoxville, TN 37902, in the City-County Building. The main line is 865-215-2330, the records department answers at 865-215-2329, and the counter serves the public on weekdays, eight until half past four. The Register of Deeds website describes the office as a recording agency only. It records deeds, deeds of trust, liens, lien releases, powers of attorney, bonds and plats, but it cannot write a deed or answer legal questions.

Each county records only the real estate inside its own lines, so a Knox County deed for a house in another county will be turned away. The office says the earliest handwritten records go back to the late 1700s, and all records except military discharges are public.

Searches usually start with the owner's name, the legal description and an approximate recording date. A title company or abstractor is still needed to confirm that title is clear, because not every lien, easement or court judgment is filed in this office.

Which fees and taxes apply to a deed filed in Knox County?

Recording fees follow Tennessee statute, and the county's fee schedule lists them. For a warranty, quitclaim or trust deed the schedule shows $12.00 covering two pages and $5.00 for each page beyond that. Taxable documents pick up another $1.00. A certified copy is $1.00 per page. The office also offers a fee calculator to estimate the total before you file.

Knox County Register of Deeds charges for common real estate filings
ItemChargeSource
Deed, up to 2 pages$12.00Knox County Register of Deeds fee schedule
Each added page$5.00Knox County Register of Deeds fee schedule
Property transfer tax$0.37 per $100Knox County Register of Deeds fee schedule
Mortgage tax$0.115 per $100, first $2,000 exemptKnox County Register of Deeds fee schedule
Plat map$17.00Knox County Register of Deeds fee schedule
Certified copy$1.00 per pageKnox County Register of Deeds fee schedule

A worked example shows the scale. On a $300,000 sale the transfer tax is $1,110, and a two-page deed adds $12.00 plus the $1.00 added fee. A $240,000 deed of trust is taxed on $238,000, which is $273.70 at the mortgage rate, plus its own recording fee. These are illustrations of the posted rates; the office's calculator and the closing agent give the real figures.

What must a Knox County deed include to be accepted?

The filing requirements page lists what warranty, quitclaim and trustee's deeds need. Rejections for missing items are the most common delay, so run through this list before the deed leaves the closing table:

  • The property must be in Knox County, and the preparer's name and full address must appear
  • Seller signatures must be notarized, and the office says an original must be presented
  • The new owner's name and address, plus the responsible taxpayer, must be shown
  • Value and consideration must be stated, and the value is taxable
  • A reference to the prior deed by instrument number or book and page, and a legal description

A warranty deed may show $0.00 consideration only between spouses, for an exempt entity, or when property goes into a revocable living trust. A trustee's deed or substitute trustee's deed must carry a trust deed reference and an appointment reference. The office also lists reasons it rejects documents: names too faint to index, a copied notary seal, a missing exhibit, or a missing chain of title.

Signatures can be notarized or witnessed by two people, with a notary the preferred method. The office accepts plats in two sizes only, 24 by 36 inches and 18 by 24 inches.

How long does recording take, and is there a deadline?

Documents are generally recorded the day they arrive. The staff checks that the document is recordable and the fees are right, assigns an instrument number, scans it, indexes it and verifies the data, which usually takes a day, and then the original goes back to the filer. Tennessee sets no time limit to record a deed, but the office advises recording as soon as possible, since leaving a deed unrecorded invites legal trouble.

The website has a page for e-recording, a request form for deed copies and a lien release form. After a mortgage is paid, the lender files a release with the register, and a copy can be obtained from the office. A lost deed is not a crisis, because the recording is the primary evidence of ownership and a certified copy acts as the original.

A change in ownership generally needs a new deed recorded in this office. Court cases such as probate, divorce or foreclosure, or certain deaths where the right language exists and a death certificate is recorded, are the exceptions to that rule. Adding or removing a name on a deed also takes a newly prepared and recorded deed, and the office suggests an attorney or title company prepare it.

What protections and reports does the Knox County office offer?

Property fraud is a live concern in county records, and the office runs a free Fraud Notification System at alertme.knoxrod.org. Owners enter their names and receive an email whenever a document under a matching name is recorded.

The office also publishes reports that help a seller price and time a sale:

  • A weekly real estate transfers report, sortable by value, with an email signup
  • Reports on money borrowed against real estate and taxes collected on mortgage records and transfers
  • A top lenders report listing every lender, the amount loaned and the number of loans in Knox County
  • Historic tax maps from the 1950s and 1980s, plus a legacy deed search

Military discharge papers, known as DD214s, can be recorded with the office at no fee, and those records are confidential.

How does the Register of Deeds fit into selling a Knox County house?

Knox County covers 526 square miles around Knoxville, and Census Bureau QuickFacts counts 232,546 housing units there in 2025, 201,146 households, and 5,013 building permits issued in 2025. Median rent is $1,261 a month, and median owner costs with a mortgage run $1,589, which gives a sense of how many deeds and mortgage releases pass through the counter.

A sale there ends at this office. The deed, the transfer tax and the recording fee all go to this office, and the office suggests that an attorney or title company prepare the deed. Ask the closing agent who files it and when. The Property Assessor then updates the owner's name, which the county says can take up to a week after recording. Before the sale, a seller should ask the Trustee for any unpaid county tax so it can be cleared at closing.

More questions about Knox County, TN Register of Deeds

What will a Knox County deed filing run in fees?

The base charge is $12.00 for a deed of up to two pages, then $5.00 for every extra page, plus $1.00 on taxable documents. The property transfer tax is $0.37 for each $100 of value.

Does a Knox County deed have to be notarized?

Yes. Seller signatures must be notarized, or witnessed by two people, and the original has to be presented. The office says a notary is the preferred method.

Does Tennessee set a deadline for recording a deed in Knox County?

No. Tennessee sets no time limit, but the Register of Deeds recommends recording as soon as possible after the sale to avoid legal problems.

Can a deed carry no sale price?

Only in limited cases. A warranty deed can show $0.00 consideration between spouses, for an exempt entity, or when property is moved into a revocable living trust.

Where can I get a copy of a deed recorded in Knox County?

Request one through the Register of Deeds website or call 865-215-2329. A certified copy is $1.00 per page and acts as the original document.

Blount County by the numbers

Where is the Blount County Register of Deeds and who runs it?

The Blount County Register of Deeds is at 349 Court Street, Maryville, TN 37804, and the phone is 865-273-5880. The county's page lists Phyllis Lee Crisp as Register and office hours of Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

This is a recording office. The register's FAQ says staff do not run title searches, do not furnish forms and do not prepare documents. If you are selling a house in Blount County, the deed usually comes from a title company or a real estate attorney, and the register records it after the tax is paid.

Blount County sits in East Tennessee, with Maryville as the county seat and largest city. Alcoa, Friendsville, Rockford and Townsend are also incorporated cities, and Louisville is a town. A deed for a house in any of them is recorded at the same Court Street office, because Tennessee records land at the county level.

What does it cost to record a deed in Blount County?

The county's fee page lists a $12 base fee for a one or two page document, plus $5 for each additional page or attachment. A $1 clerk fee is added to any document that carries a taxable amount, such as a warranty deed or deed of trust.

ItemAmount listed by the county
Recording, one or two pages$12
Each added page or attachment$5

Extra reference on documents other than deeds and trust deeds$5 per reference after the first
Certification of a recorded document$1 per page ($5 for maps)
Deed transfer tax$0.37 per $100

Source: Blount County Register of Deeds fee page. Fees must be paid in advance, and the office takes cash, check, credit or debit card, or money order. Ask the register to confirm the total before you sign if the deed has attachments, since page count changes the fee.

How much is the transfer tax on a Blount County home sale?

Tennessee charges $0.37 per $100 of the sale price, or of the property's value if that is higher. The Tennessee Department of Revenue says the buyer (the grantee on the deed) is responsible for paying it, and the register collects it when the deed is recorded.

A worked example helps. The Census Bureau lists a median owner-occupied home value of $320,500 in Blount County for 2020 to 2024. On a sale at that figure, 3,205 hundreds times $0.37 comes to $1,185.85 in transfer tax. A buyer borrowing $250,000 also pays mortgage tax of $0.115 per $100 on the amount above the first $2,000, which works out to $285.20. Contracts often shift these costs, so read the purchase agreement.

The grantee must swear to the actual consideration or the value, whichever is greater, on the face of the deed in front of the register. A false statement about value is punishable as perjury under the state's rules. The state also compares values claimed on deeds against assessor values, so a very low stated price on a sale can draw an inquiry letter.

What must a deed include to be recorded in Blount County?

The register lists several requirements on the county page. A deed that misses one is likely to be turned away at the counter.

  • A Prepared By name and address on every document.
  • The district, map and parcel number, plus the responsible taxpayer's name and address and the owner's name and address.
  • Book and page references in a format such as WD508 Pg 61. The office cannot reference documents by instrument number.
  • On trust deeds, mortgages, modifications and assignments, the sentence: 'Maximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes is $____.' Even a zero amount must be written.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope if you want the original returned. The office returns originals of real estate documents after recording.

Fixing a recorded mistake takes more than a pen. Re-recording a document requires it to be signed and notarized again, unless you record a scrivener's error affidavit that attaches or references the earlier document and describes the correction. If you need a change in ownership, the register's FAQ says a new deed has to be prepared and recorded.

Which Blount County transfers are exempt from the transfer tax?

Tennessee's recordation tax manual lists transfers that carry no realty transfer tax, and several of them show up in family and estate sales. No oath of consideration is required on an exempt transfer.

  • Transfers of a leasehold estate.
  • A conveyance from one spouse to the other that creates or ends a tenancy by the entirety.
  • Deeds signed by an executor to carry out a devise in a will.
  • Divorce decrees and deeds that adjust property rights between divorcing spouses.
  • Transfers into and out of a revocable living trust by the same person or spouse.
  • Transfers to or from a government entity.

A quitclaim deed is taxed on the consideration given, but the state says tax is due on fair market value when the wording shows an intent to convey the property itself, such as 'in fee simple' or 'to have and to hold'. Ask the title agent how your deed will be read before closing.

How do you search or e-record documents in Blount County?

The register's FAQ says the documents are not on the county website. Public computers are available at 349 Court Street. Online access runs through a vendor, US Title Search Network (ustitlesearch.net, 615-223-1823), and the county tells searchers to contact that company to subscribe.

The office also accepts e-recordings through Simplifile (800-460-5657) and CSC (1-866-403-5272). Copies cost $0.50 to email each document or $0.50 per page to print. Certified copies that serve as an original are $1.00 per page. An independent service called CRS (Courthouse Retrieval) is not run by the county or the register, so errors in its data go to that company.

Foreclosure sales posted on the courthouse steps are not tracked by the register either. If a house you are selling has a lender sale pending, the lender or its trustee holds that schedule, and a title agency can confirm what is recorded against the parcel.

What should a Blount County seller know about the local housing market?

Blount County had an estimated 143,820 residents in July 2025 and 64,682 housing units, according to the Census Bureau. Land area is 558.82 square miles, and population grew 6.3 percent from the April 2020 base. Owner-occupancy is 77.0 percent, median household income is $77,365, and 2025 building permits totaled 790.

The southern part of the county lies in the Great Smoky Mountains, and Great Smoky Mountains National Park covers much of the southeast. The northern part is Ridge-and-Valley country, and the Tennessee River forms part of the northwest border with Knox County. Wikipedia lists Denso Manufacturing Tennessee as the largest employer, at about 3,000 workers, and more than 100 manufacturing plants in the county.

Public schools are run by Blount County Schools, except in Maryville and Alcoa, which operate their own systems. Maryville College is in downtown Maryville. For sellers, the practical point is that school district, city limits and park-adjacent land all vary by address, so confirm the parcel's jurisdiction before listing.

More questions about Blount County, TN Register of Deeds

What is the phone number for the Blount County Register of Deeds?

The number is 865-273-5880. The office is at 349 Court Street, Maryville, TN 37804, and the county lists hours of Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

How much does Blount County charge to record a deed?

The county lists $12 for one or two pages and $5 for each extra page, plus a $1 clerk fee on documents with a taxable amount. Transfer tax of $0.37 per $100 is charged on top of that for a sale.

Who pays the Tennessee transfer tax on a house sale?

The Tennessee Department of Revenue says the grantee, meaning the buyer on the deed, is responsible for the realty transfer tax. A purchase contract can still assign the cost differently between buyer and seller.

Can I look up Blount County deeds online?

Yes, through a vendor. The register's page points to ustitlesearch.net, which requires a subscription. Free computers for searching are available in the office at 349 Court Street.

Does the Blount County register prepare my deed or check my title?

No. The register's FAQ states the office is a recording office that does not do title searches, furnish forms or prepare documents. Use a title company or an attorney for the deed and the title search.

The same building houses the Assessor of Property in Room 206 and the Trustee in Room 107, which makes it easy to check a parcel's value and tax status on the way to or from the recording counter.

The register's county page says the office records more than 30,000 legal documents in a typical fiscal year and handles over eighty types of instrument under the recording statutes.

What is it like to sell a house in Sumner County?

Sumner County is on Tennessee's northern edge, 25 miles northeast of Nashville. Its 543 square miles hold eight cities: Gallatin, the county seat, Hendersonville, Goodlettsville, Millersville, Mitchellville, Portland, Westmoreland and White House. Bledsoe Creek State Park sits on Old Hickory Lake, part of the Cumberland River system that shaped early trade here.

The county was organized in 1786, and the early forts at Mansker's Station, Bledsoe's Station and Asher's Station anchored its first settlements. Volunteer State Community College and a Union University campus in Hendersonville add to the local base.

Census Bureau QuickFacts for the market side:

  • 215,538 people in July 2025, up 9.8% since April 2020
  • 89,138 housing units, with 72.0% owner-occupied
  • Median owner-occupied value of $393,100 (2020 to 2024)
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage of $1,831
  • 3,045 building permits in 2025

At the median value, Tennessee's $0.37-per-$100 transfer tax would come to about $1,454 on a sale in Sumner County.

What records can I search through the Sumner County register?

The register's office says its records are certified back to September 1989 and searchable online at ustitlesearch.net. Deed books and indexes going back to 1786 have been digitized, so an older chain of title can be traced without a trip to Gallatin. A public search room is also open at the office.

Free fraud monitoring is available through MyLandAlert, which the register runs with ProGResS, Inc. It emails an owner when a document is recorded under his or her name or business, an early warning for forged deeds and mortgage fraud.

Can a Sumner County deed be e-recorded?

Yes, through two vendors named by the register: Simplifile, Inc. and CSC eRecording Solutions. The office describes e-recording as faster than paper, with documents received, recorded and returned in a short time. Tennessee limits who may submit electronically to professionals such as attorneys, lenders and title companies, so a seller will normally rely on the one handling the sale.

Paper filings still work in person or by mail at Suite 201. Bring the original, signed and notarized deed with the fees. For the exact recording fee on a given document, call 615-452-3892 before you send it.

What taxes and fees apply when recording a Sumner County sale deed?

The register collects the state conveyance tax and mortgage tax together with recording fees. State taxes go to the Department of Revenue every month, and the county keeps the recording fees. The state rates are:

State recordation taxes collected at the Sumner County register

Realty transfer tax$0.37 per $100 of purchase priceTennessee Department of Revenue
Mortgage tax$0.115 per $100 of debt, first $2,000 exemptTennessee Department of Revenue

Check the purchase contract for who covers the tax. State law also lists no-tax transfers, such as an executor's deed under a will or a divorce settlement deed, and the Shelby County register's guidelines spell out that list. For a new loan the lender's deed of trust carries the mortgage tax, and the payoff release of an old loan is recorded after closing.

What does the Sumner County register need on a deed?

A recorded deed has to carry the details Tennessee Code requires, and the Shelby County register's published list shows the usual set. Typical items include:

  • Grantor and grantee names and a legal description
  • A derivation clause naming the prior recorded deed
  • Owner and tax-payer name and address, plus the preparer's name and address
  • The parcel number and, if taxable, a sworn statement of value
  • A notarized acknowledgment of the signature

The register does not draft documents or give legal advice, and a deed missing an item can be turned away. A closing attorney or title company usually checks this list.

What should I bring to the Sumner County recording counter?

Arrive with the original deed, signed and notarized, and the payment that covers both recording and any state tax. If a lender is involved, the title company usually sends the deed of trust at the same time. Write down the parcel number from the assessor's records, the prior deed's recording reference and the mailing address for the tax bill, since the deed needs all three.

After recording, the register's staff scan the document into the database, and it can be viewed online. Keep the recorded copy with your closing papers, because lenders and buyers later ask for the instrument number.

Does it matter which part of a Sumner County city the house is in?

It can. Goodlettsville lies partly in Davidson County, and Millersville, Portland and White House each reach into Robertson County. A mailing address with a Sumner city name does not prove the parcel is inside Sumner County. Confirm the county on the Assessor's property search or the deed's parcel number before choosing a register's office, and ask the title company which county will receive the filing.

Gallatin grew near Asher's Station, a fort Captain William Asher built along Station Camp Creek in the early 1780s. Today the county seat holds the offices a seller visits to record, value and pay tax on a house.

How does Sumner County compare with other Tennessee counties for sellers?

The Census numbers set Sumner County apart from the other two large Tennessee counties covered in this series. Its median owner-occupied value of $393,100 is well above Shelby County's $249,100 and Sullivan County's $213,300, and its median household income of $90,301 is the highest of the three. Population growth since 2020 is 9.8 percent, while Shelby lost 2.1 percent.

For a seller, higher values mean larger recording taxes, since the $0.37-per-$100 rate scales with price. The recording fee itself stays small in comparison, so the tax drives the closing-table total.

How does the register connect to Sumner County property tax?

Recording a deed updates the owner of record but does not pay anything. Sumner County taxes become due the first Monday in October and are delinquent after February 28. Ask the Trustee at 615-452-1260 for the parcel balance before closing, and tell the Assessor at 615-452-2412 where the new owner wants the bill mailed.

More questions about Sumner County, TN Register of Deeds

What are the Sumner County Register of Deeds hours?

The counter opens at 8:00 and closes at 4:30 on weekdays, at 355 N. Belvedere Drive, Suite 201, Gallatin. Call 615-452-3892.

Does Sumner County offer e-recording?

Yes. The register accepts e-recorded documents through Simplifile, Inc. and CSC eRecording Solutions. Most sellers will use a title company that already has an account.

How far back do Sumner County online records go?

The register's records are certified back to September 1989 and searchable online. Deed books and indexes back to 1786 have been digitized.

What is the transfer tax on a Sumner County sale?

Tennessee charges $0.37 per $100 of the purchase price, collected by the register when the deed is recorded. On a $400,000 sale that is $1,480.

Can I get alerts about filings under my name in Sumner County?

Yes. MyLandAlert is free and emails you when a document is recorded under your name or business.

Where is the Sevier County Register of Deeds and how do I reach it?

The phone number is 865.453.2758, the fax is 865.453.0290, and the email listed on the county page is register@seviercountytn.org. The Register shown on the county site is Cyndi Pickel.

Selling a home usually means visiting more than one counter, and the courthouse keeps them close together. The Property Assessor is in Suite 210 West, the Trustee is in Room 212W, the Clerk and Master is in Suite 108 W, and the County Clerk is in Suite 202E. A seller who needs a deed recorded, a tax payoff and an ownership update can finish all three in one trip, and the office also accepts documents by mail.

What does the Sevier County Register of Deeds actually record?

The office records every document the law requires or allows to be recorded against real estate, and it indexes and stores them under statutory rules. In practice that means deeds, deeds of trust, mortgages, amendments, assignments, releases and similar papers. The county's Register of Deeds page also says the office keeps a record of the fees, commissions and taxes it collects.

Documents are cited by book and page. The county's own example looks like T508 Pg 61 or Bk 1411 Pg 32, and a title examiner will use that format to trace how a parcel passed from one owner to the next. Land records can be searched through the link on the page. After recording, the Assessor updates ownership and tax maps from the recorded deed, which is how the next tax bill finds the new owner.

Why does the county's age and layout matter for deed research?

Sevier County was formed in 1794 from part of Jefferson County and has kept its original boundaries since. It is named for John Sevier, the first governor of Tennessee, and Sevierville has been the county seat since 1795. Because the lines never moved, a long chain of title for an older farm or mountain tract stays inside one set of land books.

The county measures 598 square miles and borders Jefferson, Cocke, Blount and Knox counties in Tennessee and Haywood and Swain counties in North Carolina. A parcel near a border can still require a check of the neighboring county's records for easements or older surveys, so ask a title examiner which indexes to search before you list.

What do recording fees and taxes come to for a Sevier County deed?

The page lists a flat $12.00 for a deed, deed of trust or mortgage of up to two pages, plus a tax that depends on the price. Amendments, modifications, assignments and releases carry the same $12.00 for two pages. The full schedule from the county:

Sevier County Register of Deeds fees and taxes (county Register of Deeds page)

Blanket assignments and releases are limited to 25 per instrument. As an example, a $320,000 sale produces $1,184 of transfer tax, a $12.00 two-page recording fee and the $1.00 probate fee.

Who pays the state transfer tax on a Sevier County sale?

The buyer, called the grantee in the deed, pays it. The state revenue department explains that recordation tax has two parts, a realty transfer tax on transfers of real property and a mortgage tax on instruments that show debt. The county Register collects both and passes them on to the state.

The realty transfer tax applies to most transfers, with certain exceptions, because the buyer is asking to have the deed placed on record. Mortgage tax falls on the borrower. When a purchase is financed, a Sevier County closing therefore shows two separate taxes at recording: the transfer tax on the sale price and the mortgage tax on the loan. Read the settlement statement to see how each tax was assigned in your contract.

How do I record documents by mail in Sevier County?

Send the document, with a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself, to the Sevier County Register of Deeds, 125 Court Avenue, Suite 209W, Sevierville, TN 37862. Originals are always returned after recording, and the stamped envelope lets the office send them back without delay. Before mailing, check the following:

  • Trust deeds, mortgages, modification agreements and assignments must carry the statement "Maximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes is $____."
  • Enclose payment for the recording fee and the taxes that apply to the document.
  • Count the pages so the per-page charge is correct.
  • Make sure the legal description and parties match the prior deed in the chain of title.

Questions about a particular instrument are best settled by phone at 865.453.2758 before the packet goes in the mail.

How can I guard against deed fraud in Sevier County?

The office offers a name alert. An owner registers a name or business, and the Register notifies that person if a document is filed under it. The county's page says this lets owners recognize and stop fraudulent transactions right away. The page also notes that, as of March 3, 2025, the property fraud and online records links moved to new web addresses, so use the links on the county page, not bookmarks saved earlier.

The alert suits owners of vacation cabins, inherited houses and vacant parcels that nobody watches day to day. Sevier County, with about 101,342 residents, a $299,000 median value for owned homes and 1,139 building permits in 2025 according to Census QuickFacts, sees steady recording activity, which makes an unexpected filing easy to miss without an alert.

What should I handle besides recording when selling a Sevier County house?

Recording is the last step of a closing, and tax is the first thing to clear. The Trustee in Room 212W bills the owner of record and accepts partial payments. Taxes are payable from October 1 until the end of February, and monthly interest of 1.5 percent applies afterward. If the account is delinquent, the Clerk and Master handles the case, and the owner has one year to redeem after a tax sale.

The Assessor in Suite 210 West uses January 1 as the assessment date and updates ownership from recorded deeds. A short checklist for the days before closing:

  • Call the Trustee for a payoff figure close to the closing date.
  • Give the closing agent a copy of your current deed.
  • Ask the Register's office about any unusual instrument before you sign.

More questions about Sevier County, TN Register of Deeds

What does one deed recording cost in Sevier County?

Twelve dollars covers up to two pages, and each added page or attachment costs $5.00. Transfer tax, at 37 cents on every hundred dollars of price, is billed on top, along with a $1.00 probate fee.

Does the Sevier County Register of Deeds return my original?

Yes. Originals of real estate documents are always returned after recording. With a mailed packet, enclose a stamped envelope carrying your own address so the recorded copy can come back quickly.

What is the Sevier County mortgage tax?

$0.115 per $100 of debt, with the first $2,000 of indebtedness exempt. It is paid by the borrower when a mortgage or deed of trust is recorded, and the instrument must state the maximum principal indebtedness for recording tax purposes.

How do I search Sevier County land records?

Use the Search Land Records link on the county Register of Deeds page. Records are cited by book and page. Call 865.453.2758 for help locating an older instrument or a document that does not appear online.

Can I be notified if someone files a document in my name?

Yes. The Register of Deeds offers a name registration that sends an alert when a document is filed under your name or business. The county uses it to help owners spot and stop fraudulent filings quickly.

Where is the Bradley County Register of Deeds?

The Bradley County Register of Deeds is at 155 N. Ocoee Street, Suite 102, Cleveland, TN 37311, and the phone is 423-728-7240. The county's page names Missy Mathews as Register.

Recording in Tennessee happens at the county level, so a deed for any house in Bradley County goes to this one office, whether the property is in Cleveland, in Charleston or in the unincorporated hills between them. The county page does not post a fee schedule or hours, so call before you drive over with a deed, and ask for the total recording charge for your page count.

How do you search Bradley County land records online?

Bradley County points searchers to TitleSearcher, a vendor site that the county says gives online access to land records 24 hours a day, seven days a week. The images and index data cover deeds, mortgages, releases, powers of attorney, restrictions, plat maps and other document types filed at the register's office.

The register's page also links a property fraud alert sign-up. Fraud alerts watch for new filings under your name, which matters if you own rental property, inherited land or a vacant lot that you rarely visit. Someone who forges a deed against an empty house tends to count on the owner not noticing.

Before listing, pull the vesting deed for your parcel and check three things: the spelling of every owner name, the legal description, and any deed of trust that was never released. A lender that was paid off but did not file a release leaves a cloud on title, and a closing agent will ask you to clear it.

What taxes apply when a deed is recorded in Bradley County?

The taxes are set by state law and apply in every Tennessee county. The Tennessee Department of Revenue lists a realty transfer tax of $0.37 per $100 and a mortgage tax of $0.115 per $100 of indebtedness, with the first $2,000 of the debt exempt.

ItemRule

Who pays itThe grantee (buyer) named on the deed
Mortgage tax$0.115 per $100 of debt, first $2,000 exempt, paid by the borrower

Source: Tennessee Department of Revenue, Recordation Tax Manual. On a $230,000 sale, the transfer tax is 2,300 hundreds times $0.37, or $851. That example is arithmetic, not a quote from Bradley County, so ask the title agent for the exact charge on your deal.

Who is exempt from the Tennessee realty transfer tax?

The state manual excludes a short list of transfers. Several are common in estates, divorces and family moves, which are situations where sellers often call a buyer for a fast sale.

  • Deeds an executor signs to carry out a devise in a will.
  • Domestic settlement decrees and deeds that adjust property rights between divorcing parties.
  • A conveyance from one spouse to the other that creates or dissolves a tenancy by the entirety.
  • Transfers into a revocable living trust by the person who made it, and transfers back to that person or the spouse.
  • Real estate formerly held by tenants in common, and the release of a life estate to the remainder beneficiaries.
  • Transfers to or from a government entity.

No oath of consideration is needed on an exempt transfer. On a taxable deed, the buyer swears to the price or value on the face of the deed in front of the register, and the state can check that figure against the assessor's value later.

How does Bradley County assess value for the oath on a deed?

For a sale between unrelated parties, the price paid is the usual figure. The state accepts the tax base listed at the local assessor's office, or a recent appraisal the assessor has accepted, as the fair market value when value drives the tax. Anything lower can be audited, assessed and charged penalties and interest.

The Bradley County Assessor of Property, Stanley Thompson, is at the Courthouse Annex, 155 Broad Street NW, Room 105, and the phone is 423-728-7125. The office runs a Tennessee property viewer for parcel data and tax maps. Check the assessor's number for your house before you sign a deed that states a value far from it.

What state rules affect a deed or deed of trust recorded in Bradley County?

The Department of Revenue manual sets several rules that the Bradley County register applies at the counter. Knowing them ahead of time keeps a closing from stalling on a technicality.

  • A person who obtains several deeds for the same tract in one transfer pays the transfer tax only once, and no tax is due until title passes by deed.
  • A modified or amended deed or deed of trust should carry the book and page of the earlier document, so the register can see that tax was already paid.
  • Every instrument that evidences debt must state the maximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes, and the register may not record it until that statement is supplied and the tax is paid.
  • An assumption agreement where the buyer promises to pay the debt while the seller stays liable creates no new debt, so no mortgage tax is due. A new contract that cancels the seller's obligation does create new debt and is taxed.
  • Tax paid in another jurisdiction is proved by naming that jurisdiction and giving the book and page of the recorded document.

For a house with a payoff, ask the lender how and when it will file the release of its deed of trust. The release is what clears the record, and a buyer's title agent will look for it.

What is Bradley County like for someone selling a house?

The Census Bureau estimates 115,465 residents in July 2025 and 47,861 housing units on 328.76 square miles of land. Median owner-occupied home value for 2020 to 2024 is $261,900, owner-occupancy is 67.3 percent, and median household income is $66,552. Median gross rent is $1,030, which matters for a landlord weighing a sale against holding.

Cleveland is the county seat and largest city. Charleston is the other city, and the Hiwassee River forms the county's northern border. Wikipedia notes that the Cherokee Agency moved to Charleston in 1821, that Cleveland was chosen as county seat in 1836 and that the county ranks second in Tennessee for poultry and broilers. Whirlpool, Mars, Procter and Gamble and Duracell are among the manufacturers it names around Cleveland.

Public schools split between Bradley County Schools and Cleveland City Schools. Lee University and Cleveland State Community College are in the county. Ridges run north-northeast through the county, and Candies Creek Ridge crosses Cleveland, so lots on slopes need a careful survey and drainage check before a buyer's lender signs off.

More questions about Bradley County, TN Register of Deeds

What is the address of the Bradley County Register of Deeds?

The office is at 155 N. Ocoee Street, Suite 102, Cleveland, TN 37311. The phone is 423-728-7240, and the county's page names Missy Mathews as Register.

Can I search Bradley County deeds from home?

Yes. The county directs people to TitleSearcher, which offers land record images and index data around the clock. The register's page also links a property fraud alert sign-up.

How much is the transfer tax in Bradley County?

It is $0.37 per $100 of the sale price or value, the same in every Tennessee county. The buyer named on the deed is responsible for it, and the register collects it at recording.

Do I pay mortgage tax if I sell for cash?

No mortgage tax applies when no loan is recorded. The tax is $0.115 per $100 of debt above the first $2,000 and is charged on instruments such as a deed of trust. A cash purchase has no deed of trust.

Does the register fix errors in my deed?

The register records documents as they are presented. Ask the title company or attorney who drafted the deed how to correct it, and call 423-728-7240 to confirm what the office needs to accept the corrected version.

How much transfer tax does a Hamilton County home sale owe?

Which Hamilton County transfers are exempt from transfer tax?

  • A property adjustment ordered in a divorce.
  • A transfer under a will, called a testamentary devise.
  • A transfer made under a revocable living trust, and a release of a life estate.
  • A division in kind between tenants in common.
  • Transfers to government entities.

The county's home page also warns that a deed on death is not recognized in Tennessee, so a document of that type cannot be recorded in Hamilton County. If you inherited a house, ask the office what it will accept before you bring anything.

What changed for affidavits recorded in Hamilton County in 2026?

Since April 27, 2026, an affidavit offered for recording in Tennessee needs two separate statements, each with its own notary. The change comes from an amendment to Tenn. Code Ann. 66-24-101, and the Hamilton County register posts it as a standing notice.

  1. A jurat under 66-24-101(g) that swears the contents are true. The register must reject the document if it is missing.
  2. An acknowledgment, or two witnesses, under 66-22-101 confirming that each signer is who they claim to be.
  3. Both statements are needed for every signature on the document.

Sellers who record an affidavit of heirship, a correction affidavit or a similar paper before closing should have the notary read this notice first.

How do I e-record or search Hamilton County land records?

The register points electronic filers to two vendors. Simplifile can be reached at (800) 460-5657, and Corporation Service Company at (866) 652-0111 or through eRecording.com.

Searching the database online is a separate step. You complete a print or online application, and the $50 fee, a monthly access fee, must be paid before passwords go out. The office also publishes an instructions PDF for the record search, a document requirement guide, a public records policy and request form, and a monthly report of the property transactions recorded the month before.

If you only need one deed, a certified copy costs $1.00 per page for deeds and $5.00 per page for plats. Call 423-209-6560 for questions about a specific instrument.

Who handles property tax for a Hamilton County house after the deed is recorded?

Recording a deed does not settle the tax bill. The register's pages link to the Hamilton County Assessor of Property, the Hamilton County Trustee's online property search, and the City of Chattanooga property tax site, where city and county bills can be searched and paid. Chattanooga says no registration is needed to look up a bill.

If your house is in Chattanooga, expect both a county and a city bill. If it is in another part of the county, ask the Trustee which municipal bill, if any, applies. Before closing, ask the title company to check both searches so unpaid tax is paid from your proceeds and does not follow the house.

What should sellers know about Hamilton County itself?

Hamilton County covers 576 square miles in southeast Tennessee, with Chattanooga as the county seat on the Tennessee River and the Georgia line to the south. Other incorporated places include Collegedale, East Ridge, Lakesite, Red Bank, Ridgeside, Soddy-Daisy, Lookout Mountain, Signal Mountain and Walden. It borders ten counties, and I-24 and I-75 both run through it.

The county was created on October 25, 1819, and Chattanooga became the county seat in 1870. Hamilton County Schools is the largest school district in the state.

For 2025 the Census Bureau estimates 390,833 residents, up from 366,207 in 2020. For 2020-2024 the same agency reports that owners live in 63.9% of homes, rent runs a median $1,253, and households earn a median $76,183. Public schools are run by Hamilton County Schools, the largest district in the state.

More questions about Hamilton County, TN Register of Deeds

What is the phone number for the Hamilton County Register of Deeds?

The number is 423-209-6560, and the fax is 423-209-6561. The office is at 625 Georgia Avenue, room 400, Chattanooga, and keeps weekday hours of eight to four, closing on listed holidays.

Who pays the transfer tax on a Hamilton County deed?

The buyer named as grantee pays it, according to the Tennessee Department of Revenue. The rate is $0.37 per $100, and the register collects it at filing. A purchase contract can still assign the cost differently between buyer and seller, so read yours.

Can I record a deed on death in Hamilton County?

No. The register states that deeds on death are not recognized in Tennessee and cannot be recorded. Ask the office what it will accept for an inherited property.

Does Hamilton County accept electronic recording?

Yes, through vendors the register names: Simplifile at (800) 460-5657 and Corporation Service Company at (866) 652-0111. Ask your title company whether it submits that way.Call the office to ask about filing in person.

A certified copy of a deed is $1.00 per page, and a certified plat is $5.00 per page, under the county's published schedule. Plain copies are $0.15 per page. Confirm the amounts with the fee calculator, since the PDF is dated 2020.

Putnam County by the numbers

Where is the Putnam County Register of Deeds and what does it do?

The office sits in Room 3 of the Putnam County Courthouse at 300 E Spring St, Cookeville, TN 38501. It is open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, and the phone is 931-526-7101. The county site lists John Sanders as Register.

This office records land deeds, mortgages, releases, plats, powers of attorney and liens, including judgment liens, materialman's liens and state and federal tax liens. The county says its records reach back to 1854, the year Putnam County was re-established after an earlier version was dissolved by the courts. Anyone can ask for a copy of a recorded document in person, by phone, by mail or by email, except military discharge papers (DD-214), which are not public.

The staff will help work out a fee, but they cannot draft a deed for you. If you sell a Putnam County house, a title company or attorney normally prepares the deed, and the register records it once the tax is paid.

What does it cost to record a deed in Putnam County?

The county's fee schedule charges by the thousand dollars for deeds and trust deeds, plus per-page and flat fees. Documents filed electronically carry an extra $2.00 fee, in place since July 1, 2023.

How much is the transfer tax on a Putnam County home sale?

Tennessee's realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100, and the state Department of Revenue describes the base as the purchase price. Its help desk adds that the tax generally uses the greater of the price paid or the property's value, under Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409. The county's warranty deed line of $3.70 per thousand is the same rate written another way.

Here is a worked case. The Census Bureau lists a median owner-occupied value of $282,500 in Putnam County for 2020 to 2024. On a sale at that figure, the transfer tax is 2,825 hundreds times $0.37, or $1,045.25. Add the page fees ($10 for two pages), the $1.00 clerk fee and the $2.00 EDP fee, and the deed costs $1,058.25 to record.

A buyer who finances $225,000 also pays the indebtedness tax of $0.115 per $100 after the first $2,000, which is $256.45. Recording the trust deed brings that to $269.45 with the same flat fees. The purchase contract and your title agent will say who carries each charge.

What must a document include to be recorded in Putnam County?

The register lists seven requirements. A document that misses one will not be accepted at the counter.

  • It must be the original or a certified copy.
  • It must state who prepared it.
  • The grantor and grantee must be named.
  • The date of signing must appear.
  • A deed must carry an Oath of Consideration.
  • A deed of trust must state the maximum principal indebtedness.
  • A notary statement and notary seal must be present.

The oath matters because the tax is based on it. Fill in the real price or value, and let the title agent review the figure before anyone signs.

How do you research a property or guard against deed fraud in Putnam County?

You can search records in person at the courthouse, or online through US Title Search, which charges a monthly fee. The office can also look up the year a house was built from its tax card, and the Assessor's Office holds the same detail.

The register promotes My Land Alert, a free service at mylandalert.com that sends an email when a document is recorded in your name or your business name. Owners who rent out a house or live elsewhere should consider it. An alert gives you days, not years, to spot a deed you did not sign.

How do you change or correct a deed in Putnam County?

You cannot edit a recorded deed at the counter. To add or remove a name, you need a new deed prepared by an attorney or title agency, then recorded with the proper oath and fees.

Owners may write their own deed under Putnam County's FAQ, but the register does not recommend it and cannot help prepare one. A homemade deed that omits a required line gets turned away, and that can hold up a closing. When a mortgage is paid off, the lender sends the release to the register, and you can ask for a copy once it is recorded.

How did Putnam County get its shape?

The state first created the county in 1842 from parts of Jackson, Overton, Fentress and White counties. Overton and Jackson counties won an injunction, and a chancellor dissolved Putnam in 1845 because the new county cut their areas below constitutional limits. The legislature re-established it in 1854, and the act named the county town Cookeville for Richard F. Cooke, a state senator.

White Plains, near modern Algood, served as the temporary seat. The county is named for Israel Putnam, a general of the Revolutionary War. Caves in the Calfkiller Valley held saltpeter mines in the War of 1812 and the Civil War. Water leaves the county by three routes: tributaries of the Caney Fork in the south, the Obey River in the northeast, and Cordell Hull Lake in the north and west. Burgess Falls sits near the White County line.

The register's books start in 1854, so a title agent can trace a Putnam County parcel back to the year the county was re-established.

What shapes house sales around Cookeville and the rest of Putnam County?

Putnam County covers 403 square miles and runs on Central Time. Seven counties touch it: Overton, Fentress, Cumberland, White, DeKalb, Smith and Jackson. Cookeville is the county seat and the largest city, and Algood is the other city. Baxter and Monterey are towns. A deed for a house in any of them goes to the same courthouse office.

Tennessee Technological University is in Cookeville, and the student body is reported at about 11,800. The Census Bureau puts the county at 86,612 people on July 1, 2025, up 8.4 percent from the 2020 base. It counts 38,375 housing units, a 61.2 percent owner-occupancy rate, a median rent of $908 and a median household income of $58,912. Builders took out 629 permits in 2025. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,450, and owners without one report $446. The county counts 4,146 veterans, which is one reason the free DD-214 filing exists.

More questions about Putnam County, TN Register of Deeds

How much does it cost to record a warranty deed in Putnam County?

The county charges $3.70 per thousand dollars of value, $5.00 per page with a two-page minimum, a $1.00 clerk fee and a $2.00 EDP fee. On a $282,500 sale that totals $1,058.25 for a two-page deed.

Who is the Putnam County Register of Deeds and where is the office?

John Sanders is listed as Register. The office is in Room 3 of the Putnam County Courthouse, 300 E Spring St, Cookeville, TN 38501, and the number is 931-526-7101.

Do I need an Oath of Consideration to record a deed in Putnam County?

Yes. The register's checklist says deeds must include an Oath of Consideration, and deeds of trust must state the maximum principal indebtedness.

Can I get a copy of someone else's deed in Putnam County?

Yes. Every recorded document is public except DD-214 discharge papers, and you can request copies in person, by phone, by mail or by email.

Can I add or remove a name on my Putnam County deed myself?

A new deed is required, and the register says an attorney or title agency should prepare it. The office cannot help write the deed and does not recommend doing it yourself.

Where is the Anderson County Register of Deeds office?

The office sits at 100 North Main Street, Room 205, in Clinton, TN 37716-3624. The phone number is 865-457-6235, and the county lists office hours of Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. This is the office that records Anderson County deeds, deeds of trust and related land records and sits in the same building as the county's trustee and assessor.

Anderson County was early to put its land records online. Its register of deeds website says the office was the first in the country to offer its indexes and images over the internet, starting March 24, 1997. Charges for that access were later dropped, and the site lists indexes and images as complete from January 1, 1990 to the present. A seller or buyer can look up a recorded deed, a lien or a prior owner's name from home before ever visiting the courthouse.

Two other offices at that address matter to most sellers. The Assessor of Property is in Suite 202 (865-457-6225), and the Trustee, who collects county property tax, is in Room 203 (865-457-6233). The county's register of deeds page is the place to confirm hours before a trip.

What is Anderson County like for a home seller?

Anderson County covers 345 square miles in East Tennessee, of which 337 are land, and it belongs to the Knoxville metropolitan area. Clinton is the county seat, while Oak Ridge is the largest city. Norris, Rocky Top and Oliver Springs also lie inside the county, with Oak Ridge, Rocky Top and Oliver Springs shared with neighboring counties.

The housing stock reflects the county's history. Norris Dam, the first dam built by the Tennessee Valley Authority, went up between 1933 and 1936, and the town of Norris was planned to house its workers. During World War II the federal Manhattan Project founded Oak Ridge in 1942. Tourism is a visible part of the economy, with Norris Lake, the Museum of Appalachia and the American Museum of Science and Energy among the draws.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts for the county show how the market looks on paper:

  • 82,066 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up 6.3% from April 2020

What does a deed need before the Anderson County register will record it?

The register's job is to decide whether a document is acceptable for recording. Legal sufficiency falls outside that job, and a deed that misses a required item can be turned away. According to the University of Tennessee County Technical Assistance Service's register of deeds training materials, a deed must meet these requirements under Tennessee law:

  • Be legible and authenticated, with an original signature and a notarial acknowledgment or an equivalent certificate
  • Show the name and address of the owner and the taxpayer (T.C.A. 66-24-114)
  • Include a derivation clause that refers to the earlier recorded deed (66-24-110)
  • Show the name and address of the person who prepared it (66-24-115)
  • Carry the parcel identification number (66-24-122)
  • Arrive with the required fees and any transfer or mortgage tax

Most of these are checked at the closing table by the title company or attorney who prepares the deed. An owner who is selling without an agent can bring the draft to the register's office with a phone call ahead of time, which helps catch a missing parcel number before the buyer is waiting on it.

How much is the Tennessee transfer tax on an Anderson County sale?

Tennessee charges a realty transfer tax of $0.37 per $100, set by T.C.A. 67-4-409, and the county register collects it when the deed is recorded. The grantee, meaning the buyer, is responsible for paying it. The tax is generally based on the greater of the price paid or the value of the property. At the county's $239,400 median home value, the tax would be about $886.78, though a real sale is taxed on its own price or value.

The buyer or the buyer's agent swears to the value on the face of the deed in front of the register. A knowingly false statement is treated as perjury, and the Department of Revenue compares deed values against assessor records in its discovery reviews. An oath is not required on an exempt transfer.

The Department of Revenue lists transfers that owe no realty transfer tax. They include transfers between spouses that create or end a tenancy by the entirety, deeds an executor signs to carry out a will, divorce decrees and settlement deeds, and transfers to or from a revocable living trust by the same person or spouse. A transfer to or from a government entity is also exempt.

What other recording costs come with a deed in Anderson County?

A $2.00 computer fee is added to non-UCC instruments, and a register with county legislative body approval may charge $2.00 for documents filed through the county's electronic portal. Government filers are exempt from that e-filing fee.

A new mortgage adds the mortgage tax, which the borrower pays. A document with several instruments, such as a deed plus a release of an old deed of trust, is charged $5.00 for each added instrument. The register also may not take payment for services other than those the law lists, and fees must accompany the document.

When a lender is paying off an old loan at closing, the release is usually recorded after the sale. Ask the title company who submits it, and whether that submission includes a fee.

How does recording connect to property tax when selling in Anderson County?

Recording a deed changes the owner of record, but it does not settle the tax bill. County property tax in Tennessee is collected by the trustee, and the assessment date is January 1 each year. The Comptroller's schedule shows that taxes become due on the first Monday in October and are delinquent on March 1 of the next year. Anderson County's trustee also runs the tax relief and tax freeze programs for the county and its cities.

A seller should ask the trustee for the status of the current and any past-due bills before closing, and ask the assessor's office how the parcel is valued. Anderson County's assessor sets an appraised value on each parcel and hears owner appeals about value. Those appeals begin at the county board of equalization and can move to the State Board of Equalization, according to the Comptroller.

An owner who is 65 or older, or who is disabled, can also ask the trustee about the state tax relief and tax freeze programs before deciding whether to sell.

More questions about Anderson County, TN Register of Deeds

Where do I record a deed in Anderson County, TN?

Record it at the Anderson County Register of Deeds, 100 North Main Street, Room 205, Clinton, TN 37716. The phone number is 865-457-6235, and the county lists weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The buyer pays it. Tennessee law puts the realty transfer tax on the grantee, at $0.37 per $100 of the greater of the price or the value. The purchase contract may say who covers closing costs, so read it before signing.

Can I search Anderson County deed records online?

Yes. The register's website at andersondeeds.com offers indexes and images from January 1, 1990 to the present, and it says access is free. The county was the first register's office in the country to offer this, starting in March 1997.

Does a transfer of a house into my living trust owe transfer tax?

Not under the Department of Revenue's list, which exempts a transfer by a person to a revocable living trust created by that person or the person's spouse, and a transfer by the trustee back to them. The deed should still meet the register's recording requirements.

Is the register of deeds the same as the property assessor?

No. The register records documents and collects the transfer tax. The Assessor of Property, in Suite 202 of the same building at 865-457-6225, sets the appraised value for tax. The Trustee in Room 203 collects the bill.

Where is the McMinn County Register of Deeds, and what does the office do?

Find the office on the main floor of the McMinn courthouse, 6 East Madison Avenue, Athens, TN 37303, or call (423) 745-1232. Cheryl Ingram is the elected Register. Counter service runs from half past eight in the morning until four in the afternoon.

Staff record conveyances, deeds of trust, leases and similar instruments, and they certify copies of anything on file. Voters choose the register countywide every four years. According to the county's register page, the counter takes debit and credit cards, with American Express excluded. That page prints no fee schedule, so ask the staff for a total when your deed runs long.

What is McMinn County like to sell in?

The legislature carved McMinn out in 1819 and named it for Joseph McMinn, a former governor. Athens serves as seat of government and is the biggest city. Etowah, Niota and Sweetwater are cities too, while Calhoun and Englewood are towns. Ridge and Valley terrain covers most of the county, and the Hiwassee River forms its southwestern edge against Bradley County.

Census QuickFacts lists 57,404 residents as of July 2025, a 7.8% gain over the April 2020 base. There are 24,424 housing units across 430 square miles of land, about 124 residents per square mile. Households earn a median $61,470, and renters pay a median $803 in gross rent.

What does recording a McMinn County deed cost in state tax?

Two state taxes apply at recording. The transfer tax is 37 cents for each $100 of the sale price or property value, whichever is higher. The mortgage tax is 11.5 cents for each $100 borrowed, and the first $2,000 of any debt is left out. Under the state's recordation tax manual the register collects both on the spot, and the grantee shown on the deed carries the transfer tax.

Try the county's Census median as a test case. A $211,800 sale is 2,118 hundreds, and 2,118 times $0.37 comes to $783.66 in transfer tax. A buyer financing $170,000 would owe mortgage tax on $168,000, or 1,680 hundreds at $0.115, which is $193.20.

What does the McMinn County register require before a deed is recorded?

McMinn County posts a checklist called Requirements to Record Documents. Any deed lacking one of its items risks rejection, so walk through it with whoever prepares your closing papers.

  • Preparer's name and address, matching the return envelope if you enclose one.
  • Grantee's address, along with the address for future tax bills.
  • Map and parcel number, legal description, and last book and page of title.
  • Each signature notarized, with the acknowledgment naming the signers and carrying the notary's seal and date.
  • A sworn oath of consideration giving whichever is larger, the price or the property's value.
  • For any document tied to debt, the sentence "Maximum principal indebtedness for TN tax recording purposes is $___."

A corrected document needs fresh signatures and acknowledgments, or a scrivener's affidavit stapled to it. The checklist also says documents sent without a stamped, self-addressed return envelope may be destroyed 90 days after recording, so include one if you want the original back.

Which McMinn County transfers owe no realty transfer tax?

Some transfers escape the $0.37 tax under the state manual, and a few matter in family and estate sales. Exempt transfers need no oath.

  • Transfers of a leasehold estate.
  • One spouse deeding to the other as a tenancy by the entirety begins or ends.
  • A deed signed by an executor to carry out a gift in a will.
  • Domestic decrees and deeds that adjust property rights between divorcing spouses.
  • Moves into or back out of a revocable living trust made by that owner or the owner's spouse.
  • Conveyances to or from a government body.

A quitclaim deed is taxed on the consideration given, yet the state taxes fair market value when its wording shows an intent to pass the property itself, such as "in fee simple." State revenue staff sometimes pull deeds from a random county and date range, set the sworn value beside the assessor's figure, and mail an inquiry letter if the two are far apart. An unusually low stated price on a McMinn County deed can draw that letter.

How do you search records or e-record documents in McMinn County?

The register accepts electronic recordings through Simplifile, Corporation Service Company (CSC) and eRecording Partners Network (EPN). Your title company will pick one of these routes at closing.

For searching, the county points researchers to US Title Search Network, which charges per search or a monthly fee. If that service gives you trouble, the register's page lists Progress Inc. at 1 (800) 394-7477. Assessor data is separate: the county's Assessor of Property, Keith Price, at (423) 745-2743, keeps parcel maps and property cards, and the state's assessment website lets you look up map and parcel numbers that every conveyance needs.

If you inherited a McMinn County house and need to sell, ask the register how the executor's deed should be worded, and ask the probate clerk for proof of authority.

Who bills the property tax when a McMinn County house sells?

County property tax goes to the McMinn County Trustee in the courthouse at 6 East Madison Avenue, phone (423) 745-1291. The current year's bill can be paid between October 1 and the end of February. Weekday hours are 8 to 4, and the office also opens on Saturday mornings in February.

The Trustee also handles applications for the state's Tax Relief Program, which helps elderly and disabled homeowners and disabled veterans. The county page sets the application cutoff at 35 days after the February 28 payment deadline. Relief repays part of a bill the owner has paid, so the bill itself still arrives.

Settlement of the current year's tax is a closing-table decision, so raise it with the closing agent early and get a payoff from the Trustee beforehand. If the owner name or mailing address on the roll is wrong, the assessor can fix it.

More questions about McMinn County, TN Register of Deeds

Where is a McMinn County deed recorded?

The McMinn County Register of Deeds does, in the Athens courthouse at 6 East Madison Avenue. Call (423) 745-1232 with questions. Title companies normally submit deeds electronically.

How much transfer tax applies when a McMinn County house sells?

Thirty-seven cents per $100 of the larger of price or value. At the county's $211,800 Census median that comes to $783.66, owed by the grantee unless the contract shifts it.

Can a deed be e-recorded in McMinn County?

Yes. The register takes e-recordings from Simplifile, CSC and eRecording Partners Network. Individuals without an account usually rely on a title company or attorney.

Is transfer tax owed on a sale of an inherited McMinn County house?

A deed an executor signs to carry out a gift in a will is exempt. The later sale to a buyer is taxed at the normal rate, so ask the register how each deed in the chain is treated.

Where is McMinn County property tax paid ahead of a closing?

Pay the McMinn County Trustee at the courthouse in Athens and call (423) 745-1291 for a payoff figure. Current-year bills are payable October 1 through the end of February.

Robertson County by the numbers

What does the Robertson County Register of Deeds do?

John West's office files the instruments that move title to land in Robertson County: warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, deeds of trust, releases and plats. The Register is elected to a four year term, keeps weekday hours of 8 to 4:30, and has no weekend service.

The office describes its own purpose in simple terms. Most residents buy a house or a tract of land at some point, it is often the biggest purchase they make, and so the accuracy of the records matters. For a seller, the deed is the paper that puts the new owner on the public record, and recording it is what prompts the Assessor to update the parcel.

What is the background of Robertson County, Tennessee?

Robertson County was organized in 1796 and carries the name of James Robertson, the explorer who founded Nashville. Springfield, the seat, was laid out in 1798, and tobacco was the main commodity crop through the nineteenth century into the early twentieth.

The county covers 476 square miles on the central northern edge of Tennessee. Kentucky's Logan, Simpson and Todd counties lie to the north, and Sumner, Davidson, Cheatham and Montgomery counties border it inside Tennessee. The 2020 census count was 72,803. Thomas Kilgore, the first European settler, arrived in 1778 at what is now Cross Plains. Interstate 65 follows the eastern border for about 20 miles and Interstate 24 runs along the southwest for about 10, while U.S. 41 and 431 cross in Springfield, and U.S. 31W passes through White House and Cross Plains along the Sumner County line.

What are the recording charges for a deed in Robertson County?

A warranty deed, quitclaim deed, deed of trust or lease is charged $5.00 for each page, with a $10.00 floor and a $2.00 electronic data processing fee on top. The Register's own $1.00 fee is added only on instruments that carry state tax.

Robertson County Register of Deeds recording fees
DocumentFeeSource
Deeds, deeds of trust, leases, liens, agreements$5.00 per page, $10.00 minimum, plus $2.00 processingRegister of Deeds fee page

Assignments$10.00 for one or two pages, $5.00 per extra page or assignment, plus $2.00Register of Deeds fee page
